chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).
Regarding the Words of God, the Exalted: 'And monasticism which they invented for themselves, We did not prescribe for them,' he said: 'It is the night prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'monasticism' (rahbaniyyah) refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) reinterprets the Quranic concept of 'monasticism' (rahbaniyyah) not as a Christian innovation, but as the voluntary night prayer (salat al-layl) practiced by the early Muslim community to seek divine pleasure. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly view that the verse critiques the self-invented asceticism of the companions, distinguishing it from the obligatory acts prescribed in the Sharia. The emphasis on night prayer highlights its role as a primary means of spiritual elevation and closeness to God in Shia piety.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-29 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Hussein ibn Abil Khattab, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdullah, on the authority of Abil Hassan (Imam Ridha) (s), “

What is meant by the following Words of the Honorable the Exalted God - ‘…But the Monasticism which they invented for themselves, We did not prescribe for them: (We commanded) only the seeking for the Good Pleasure of Allah…’  - is night prayers.”
